claims.text: Current-dollar (nominal) PCE increased $23.7 billion (0.1 percent) from the preceding month in July 2022, reflecting a $33.3 billion increase in services spending partly offset by a $9.6 billion decrease in goods spending.

citations.quotation: personal consumption expenditures (PCE) increased $23.7 billion (0.1 percent).

$23.7 billion increase in current-dollar PCE in July reflected an increase of $33.3 billion in spending
for services that was partly offset by a decrease of $9.6 billion in spending for goods (table 3).

claims.text: Within services, housing and utilities and "other" services led the increase; within goods, gasoline and other energy goods led the decrease.

citations.quotation:
Within
services, the largest contributors to the increase were spending for housing and utilities (mainly
housing) and for "other" services (mainly international travel). Within goods, gasoline and other energy
goods was the leading contributor to the decrease.

claims.text: The personal saving rate in July 2022 was 5.0 percent, with personal saving of $932.3 billion.

citations.quotation:
Personal saving was $932.3 billion in July and
the personal saving rate—personal saving as a percentage of disposable personal income—was 5.0
percent (table 1).

claims.text: Nominal PCE is distinct from the PCE price index: current-dollar PCE rose 0.1 percent while the PCE price index fell 0.1 percent; real (chained-dollar) PCE rose 0.2 percent.

citations.quotation:
The PCE price index decreased 0.1 percent. Excluding food and energy, the PCE price index increased 0.1
percent (table 9). Real DPI increased 0.3 percent in July and real PCE increased 0.2 percent; goods
increased 0.2 percent and services increased 0.2 percent
